The key pattern: Rook check on the first rank forces the king forward into a discovered attack or mating net from the queen. After the king moves, the queen delivers the next check, driving the king into a position where escape squares close off.

**Coaching note:** When the opponent's king is exposed, look for forcing moves that push it further into danger. A rook check on an open rank can be devastating—it forces the king to commit to one direction, then your other pieces (especially the queen) can cut off escape squares. The forcing sequence often matters more than material.
